Victorville Superior Court

Legal disputes can be complex and challenging, and finding the right court to handle your case can be overwhelming. In this article, we will explore the functions and operations of the Victorville Superior Court and the San Bernardino Superior Court, two of the most significant court systems in San Bernardino County, California. We will also cover their online services, case search options, and contact information.

Overview of the Victorville Superior Court

The Victorville Superior Court is one of the five divisions of the San Bernardino Superior Court, serving the residents of Victorville, Adelanto, Apple Valley, Barstow, Hesperia, and surrounding communities. The Court is responsible for handling various types of cases, including civil, criminal, family law, probate, and juvenile cases.

Victorville Superior Court Contact Information

  • Address: 14455 Civic Drive, Victorville, CA 92392
  • Phone: (760) 245-6215
  • Website: https://www.sb-court.org/Victorville

The Court’s Jurisdiction

The Victorville Superior Court has jurisdiction over cases that occur within its geographic boundaries. These boundaries cover the cities mentioned above and the unincorporated areas of San Bernardino County. The Court has the authority to hear cases that involve disputes between individuals or entities, crimes committed within its jurisdiction, and violations of state or local laws.

Types of Cases Heard in the Court

The types of cases heard in the Victorville Superior Court include:

Civil Cases

Civil cases involve disputes between individuals or entities that seek a legal remedy, such as money damages or specific performance. The types of civil cases heard in the Victorville Superior Court include:

Small Claims Cases

Small claims cases involve disputes that do not exceed $10,000 in damages. The cases are typically resolved in a simplified, informal process, without a jury or attorneys.

Limited Civil Cases

Limited civil cases involve disputes that do not exceed $25,000 in damages. The cases follow a formal process, with a jury or judge, and attorneys may represent the parties.

Unlimited Civil Cases

Unlimited civil cases involve disputes that exceed $25,000 in damages. These cases are typically more complex and may involve multiple parties or legal issues.

Criminal Cases

Criminal cases involve violations of criminal laws, such as theft, assault, or driving under the influence (DUI). The types of criminal cases heard in the Victorville Superior Court include:

Infraction Cases

Infraction cases involve minor violations of the law, such as traffic tickets. The cases are typically resolved by paying a fine, without a trial.

Misdemeanor Cases

Misdemeanor cases involve more serious violations of the law, such as petty theft or domestic violence. The cases follow a formal process, with a trial by a judge or jury, and the defendant may face fines or imprisonment.

Felony Cases

Felony cases involve the most serious violations of the law, such as murder, robbery, or drug trafficking. These cases are more complex and follow a formal process, with a trial by a judge or jury, and the defendant may face imprisonment or other severe penalties.

Family Law Cases

Family law cases involve disputes between family members or related individuals, such as divorce, child custody, or domestic violence. The Victorville Superior Court has a dedicated family law division that handles these cases.

Probate Cases

Probate cases involve the distribution of a deceased person’s assets and property. The Victorville Superior Court has a probate division that handles these cases.

Juvenile Cases

Juvenile cases involve disputes or criminal offenses committed by individuals under the age of 18. The Victorville Superior Court has a juvenile division that handles these cases.

Court Processes and Procedures

The Victorville Superior Court follows certain processes and procedures for handling cases. These include:

Filing a Case

To initiate a case, a party must file the necessary paperwork with the Court and pay the required fees. The Court provides various forms and instructions on its website.

Serving a Defendant

Once a case is filed, the plaintiff must serve the defendant with a copy of the paperwork. This can be done through various methods, such as personal service, certified mail, or publication.

Court Appearances

Parties may be required to appear in court for various hearings, such as case management conferences, pre-trial conferences, or trials. The Court provides notices and instructions for these appearances.

Mediation and Settlement Conferences

The Court offers mediation and settlement conferences as alternative dispute resolution methods to help parties reach a resolution without going to trial.

Trial and Judgment

If a case goes to trial, a judge or jury will hear the evidence and arguments presented by both parties and make a judgment. The Court will then issue a final decision or order.

Court Resources and Services

The Victorville Superior Court provides various resources and services to help parties navigate the court process. These include:

Self-Help Services

The Court offers self-help services for parties who cannot afford an attorney. These services include legal clinics, workshops, and online resources.

Interpreter Services

The Court provides interpreter services for parties who do not speak English or who are deaf or hard of hearing.

Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations

The Court offers accommodations for individuals with disabilities, such as wheelchair access, assistive listening devices, and sign language interpreters.

Court Forms and Instructions

The Court provides various forms and instructions on its website to help parties navigate the court process.

Online Services and Case Search Options

The Victorville Superior Court provides various online services and case search options for parties to access court information and records. These include:

Case Search

Parties can search for case information and records using the Court’s online case search portal. The portal provides access to case information and documents, including case summaries, filings, and orders.

Smart Search

The Court’s smart search portal allows parties to search for cases by party name, case number, or filing date. The portal provides access to case information and documents, including case summaries, filings, and orders.

Open Access Portal

The San Bernardino Superior Court’s open access portal provides access to case information and records for civil, criminal, family law, probate, and small claims cases. The portal allows parties to view case documents, register for email notifications, and request copies of documents.

Conclusion

The Victorville Superior Court and the San Bernardino Superior Court play crucial roles in providing justice and resolving disputes for the residents of San Bernardino County. These courts provide a wide range of services and resources, including self-help services, interpreter services, and online case search options, to enhance accessibility and inclusivity. Whether you need legal assistance or have a dispute that requires resolution, these courts are viable options to consider.

FAQs

How do I search for cases in the Victorville Superior Court?

  • You can search for cases using the Court’s online case search portal or smart search portal.

How do I file a case in the San Bernardino Superior Court?

  • You can file a case by completing the necessary paperwork and paying the required fees. The Court provides various forms and instructions on its website.

How do I request an interpreter for my case?

  • You can request an interpreter when filing your case or by contacting the Court.

How do I access the San Bernardino Superior Court’s open access portal?

  • You can access the portal on the Court’s website by clicking on the “Open Access Portal” link.

How do I request ADA accommodations for my court appearance?

  • You can request accommodations by contacting the Court’s ADA coordinator at least five business days before your court appearance.
